memory.fix: Kernels are now created lazily in reset() for the selected scenario only, so each env holds a single active kernel. Measured N kernels x one full episode = 243.2 KB/kernel (one-time). Rust peak RSS 1236 MB -> 905 MB; the remaining +243 MB over Python is the shared ScenarioStore (immutable tapes for 600 scenarios, measured below), which is the deliberate R4 optimization.
memory.root_cause: NativeBusDispatchEnv eagerly built one Kernel per scenario. Each kernel allocates ~243 KB of per-episode scratch on its first episode and keeps it (bounded, reused on later episodes). With 500 train scenarios x 4 envs plus 100 validation scenarios that was ~500 MB of idle per-scenario kernels. Python does not pay this because it builds WorldState only for the active scenario.

notes: Full L0-protocol seed: identical 20-point validation curve and byte-identical weights/optimizer after the memory fix, so the fix does not change training.
Rust wall time is within noise of the pre-fix run (146.95 s vs 142.97 s metadata); one repeat of the fixed run measured 176.8 s, an outlier from background load, so both fixed runs are recorded.
Checkpoint .zip sha256 values differ only by embedded object addresses and start_time; tensor members are byte-identical.

protocol.order_note: Python ran first so Rust was measured on the warmer machine (conservative).
